title: Massive Update for Costco Stock Investors
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc's September 23 video is a pre-earnings check on Costco ahead of its September 24 quarterly report, and it ends with a rare stance change: his first BUY upgrade on Costco in years (the last was around 2021/22). Context: the stock has fallen ~20% from near $1,100 to below $900, and for the first time in his years of following it the valuation looks fair rather than rich. He walks through the business: US comparable store sales up 9% in August (5.6% ex-gas, 2.8% in Canada), digitally enabled sales up 17.9%, $293 billion trailing-12-month sales from under 1,000 warehouses worldwide — dwarfing Walmart (~$700 billion from 10,000+ stores) and Target on a sales-per-store basis. He emphasizes the deliberate model: razor-thin margins (3.8% operating margin) are the strategy — savings are passed to customers, rewarded by 90%+ US membership renewal rates where the real profit sits — and industry-leading capital allocation, with inventory turning so fast Costco often sells goods before paying suppliers, driving a 22.6% return on invested capital that leads Home Depot, Walmart, and Target. His updated DCF puts fair value at $843 versus ~$897 market, only 6% overvalued and well within his margin of safety; the 36x forward P/E is near the lowest since 2024. The call: COST — BUY (upgrade), execution advice to buy half before and half after earnings since he is indifferent to timing. Bull: an earnings beat reignites the premium multiple; bear: at 36x forward a soft quarter extends the de-rating. Other tickers mentioned for comparison only: Walmart, Target, Home Depot. The video carries a Motley Fool sponsorship.
